spread.caption: Each dot is one run on one of 24 seeds no one tuned or trained on; the expert script scores 1.00.

reference.what: Adds capacity to geo-svc at minute 17, before rolling it back, so the rollback starts no storm and partner-api stays at 0%. Throttles a service only for the minute its fix lands.

moments.label: adds capacity first, then rolls back

r16-l4-s200019-opus-220058.what: Ahead of the reference until minute 33. Then it rolled back geo-svc without adding capacity first: retries overloaded it, and partner-api, which earns $29,100 a minute, went to 72% errors. Minutes 33 to 42 cost it $185,000, the reference $1,000.
r16-l4-s200019-opus-220058.source: metrics.json, round 16: one of the two Opus 5.5 runs on seed 200019, one of the 24 common seeds. Quotes are from its closing message.

moments.label: rolls back unprotected
moments.quote: I rolled it back at minute 34. That made things worse: geo-svc was already near capacity (CPU 0.85), and the failures during the rollback triggered a retry storm.
That spike cost about $175k, more than the roughly $100k that leaving the 4% until the end of the shift would have cost. Throttling or scaling geo-svc before the rollback would have prevented it.

r13-l4-s109-opus-204810.what: Level with the reference until minute 34. Then it rolled back search-svc without adding capacity first: retries overloaded it and web-storefront went to 72% errors. Minutes 34 to 46 cost it $163,000, the reference $42,000.
r13-l4-s109-opus-204810.source: metrics.json, round 13: the one Opus 5.5 run on seed 109, a seed no shipped task uses. Quotes are from its closing message.

moments.label: rolls back unprotected
moments.quote: Rolling back search-svc made 30% of its requests fail while it ran. Those failures were retried and overloaded it, which cost the most in the incident.

moments.label: adds capacity after the storm
moments.quote: Scaling search-svc up before the rollback would probably have avoided most of that.
Deploy v175 broke its rate limiter (`refill = rate * elapsed / 1000`), so it rejected most requests and retries overloaded it. I rolled it back at minute 16.

r13-l4-s108-opus-204805.what: Rolled back checkout-svc without adding capacity first: retries overloaded it and web-storefront went to 72% errors. It reached for the throttle only after the storm had started. Minutes 34 to 46 cost it $132,000, the reference $36,000.
r13-l4-s108-opus-204805.source: metrics.json, round 13: the one Opus 5.5 run on seed 108, a seed no shipped task uses. Quotes are from its closing message.

moments.label: rolls back unprotected
moments.quote: This rollback was my most expensive move. I started it while checkout-svc was already near capacity. The 30% of requests it failed set off a retry storm.

moments.label: throttles after the storm
moments.quote: Rejecting some of its traffic before starting the rollback, or adding replicas first, would have avoided most of that loss.
